This chapter builds the objects that probability theory studies on top of the measure theory of Chapter 1. Section 2.1 introduces random variables as measurable functions and describes them through their laws and distribution functions. Section 2.2 defines the expectation as a Lebesgue integral, first for simple functions and then by monotone limits, and Section 2.3 collects the inequalities that control expectations and the spaces

A random variable is a numerical quantity whose value is decided by the outcome of an experiment. To compute the probability that it falls in an interval, the set of outcomes that make it do so has to be an event. This single requirement is the whole definition.
We state the requirement for maps between two measurable spaces, since the same notion covers random vectors, random sequences, and random functions.
